t: Find the K-or of an Array
o: For each bit position, count how many numbers have that bit set; set it in the answer if the count is at least k. With n ≤ 50 and values < 2³¹, checking all 31 bits is trivial. Example 1: bit 0 appears in 4 numbers and bit 3 in 5, both ≥ k=4, giving 9.
k: K-or decomposes independently per bit position.

a.i: Iterate bit positions 0..30, count set bits across the array, and OR in the bit when the count reaches k.
s: For each bit b in 0..30, count nums[i] with bit b set
If count ≥ k, set bit b in the answer

a.i: Accumulate per-bit counters in one pass over the array, then assemble the answer — slightly fewer passes, same complexity.
s: Maintain cnt[32]; for each number increment cnt[b] for each set bit
Build answer from bits with cnt[b] ≥ k

w: Trivial problem; the only care point is using unsigned/right-shift-safe operations in JavaScript (>>> and avoiding bit 31 sign issues). k=1 reduces to ordinary OR — a good sanity check.
